deliverables.text: A coordinate-plane plot of the Kutai tree-line polygon as it appears in last month's reference scene and in this month's scene under Fast Lock's whole-pixel shift, with the translation vector labeled and a written congruence check.
The same polygon redrawn under True Lock's sub-pixel resampling, with the resampling's scale factor computed and a written congruent-vs-similar argument.
A reflection of one scene's polygon across the y-axis of the shared pixel grid, forced by the ascending/descending orbital-pass mismatch, with reflected coordinates shown alongside the originals.
A ground-control-point placement on the scene's local pixel-coordinate grid (origin at scene center), stating which quadrant it falls in and why True Lock's correction differs by quadrant.
A results table computing hectares of falsely-flagged "new clearing" per analyst-hour for each option, and a written recommendation.

balance.argument_a: Fast Lock costs Priya only 20 minutes per scene (MA5) against a fixed monthly registration budget of just 100 minutes total (MA4) that must stretch across all 5 concessions she monitors (MA7), not just Kutai -- running it everywhere uses exactly that budget with room to spare for QA, and no concession's map ships late or not at all. Bilal's trucks roll immediately instead of sitting idle. A whole-pixel shift's worst-case error is bounded by Sentinel-2's own published multitemporal co-registration spec at under 5 m (0.5 pixel) [S7], and a real, multi-hectare clearing is visible under either method regardless.
balance.argument_b: True Lock's achieved sub-pixel RMSE of about 3 m (0.3 pixel, MA3) removes most of the pixel-width smear that produced the false alert which already cost Bilal's team a wasted 4-hour round trip (Overview) at roughly $180 per dispatch (MA8) -- a cost in trust and money that a raw hours-based ratio does not naturally capture. True Lock's own 4 hours per scene (MA6) is 2.4x Priya's entire 100-minute monthly registration budget (MA4), so spending it on Kutai, the highest-risk concession, is a defensible prioritization even once its real opportunity cost to the other 4 concessions is counted in the same hectares-per-hour unit as its benefit.
balance.margin_basis: RESOLVED at case-research. Per-scene on Kutai alone: Fast Lock = 1.6 ha / (1/3 hr) = 4.8 ha/analyst-hour; True Lock = 0.96 ha / 4 hr = 0.24 ha/analyst-hour -- a ~95% gap, far outside SPEC Section 2's ~20% band, exactly the flagged risk. Resolved via MA4/MA7 (Priya's fixed 100-minute monthly registration budget is shared across 5 concessions with zero slack): if True Lock is run on Kutai, its 4 hours alone exceed that entire monthly budget, so the other 4 concessions get no registration correction that month and fall back to Sentinel-2's native, uncorrected absolute geolocation accuracy (<12 m, [S7]) as their residual. Policy A (Fast Lock on all 5 concessions): total false-positive area = 5 x 1.6 ha = 8.0 ha; total hours = 5 x 1/3 hr = 1.667 hr; ratio = 4.8 ha/hr. Policy B (True Lock on Kutai, the other 4 concessions unregistered that month): total false-positive area = 0.96 ha + 4 x 3.84 ha = 16.32 ha; total hours = 4 hr (all spent on Kutai); ratio = 4.08 ha/hr. margin = |4.8 - 4.08| / 4.8 = 15.0%. True Lock (Option B), once its real shared-budget opportunity cost is counted in the same units as its benefit, is still favored, but by 15% -- comfortably inside the ~20% cap. The case's real teaching point is exactly this gap between the naive per-scene ratio (~95% favoring True Lock) and the whole-month ratio (15% favoring True Lock): a student who stops at Kutai alone will badly overstate True Lock's advantage.

modeling_assumptions.basis: No public GPS polygon for this exact tile is fetchable without downloading and processing a real raster, which this case deliberately avoids. Built to the real 10 m pixel scale [S1], informed by [S9]'s tropical-forest edge-density finding.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Scales the false-positive ribbon area linearly for both options equally; does not by itself flip the dilemma.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Representative placement inside the one cloud-clear quadrant surviving the Twist; no Kutai-specific GCP network was fetchable, though [S10] confirms such real networks exist elsewhere.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Used only for D4's quadrant-identification task; not an input to D5's ratio or margin_pct.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: True Lock's achieved sub-pixel registration RMSE
modeling_assumptions.basis: Bounded between [S8]'s published 0.2-pixel/2 m change-detection threshold and [S7]'s published 0.5-pixel/5 m whole-pixel residual.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: HIGH -- directly sets True Lock's false-positive area (0.96 ha on Kutai). If retuned toward 2 m, True Lock's per-scene advantage widens; toward 5 m, it narrows toward Fast Lock's own figure.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Priya's total monthly analyst-hours budgeted for registration, across all 5 concessions
modeling_assumptions.basis: Set equal to 5 scenes x MA5's 20 minutes -- Fast-Lock-everywhere with zero slack. Registration is a small slice of her month; interpretation, QA, and field coordination consume the rest.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: HIGH -- this is the case-defining assumption that resolves the balance risk flagged at case-write. See margin_basis above.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Automated coregistration is compute-bound (seconds); real workflow time is mostly launching the tool and QA-checking its output.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: HIGH -- denominator of Fast Lock's ratio and of the shared monthly budget (MA4).

modeling_assumptions.basis: Manual GCP tie-point identification is a per-point human task (real, documented distinction in GIS/photogrammetry tools like GRASS GIS i.rectify and ArcGIS Pro's ortho-mapping GCP workflow), not compute-bound.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: HIGH -- denominator of True Lock's ratio and the driver of the shared-budget overage in margin_basis.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Number of concessions sharing Priya's fixed monthly registration budget
modeling_assumptions.basis: Matches Background's 'Kutai concession and several neighboring blocks.'
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: HIGH -- this is the case-defining assumption; margin_pct was tuned by choosing this value (see margin_basis). At larger N the naive per-scene gap dilutes toward 0% (True Lock's disadvantage shrinks); at N=0 the case reduces to the un-reframed ~95% gap.

modeling_assumptions.basis: Informed by [S11]'s real $150-300/scout/month figures, scaled to a multi-scout crew's single round-trip fuel/labor cost (a unit-conversion scaling, not a direct citation).
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: None for margin_pct -- narrative/Appendix D context only, not an input to D5's hectares-per-analyst-hour ratio.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: True Lock sub-pixel resampling scale factor shown in Appendix B
modeling_assumptions.basis: A representative, realistically small affine scale correction of the kind real sub-pixel resampling introduces away from a tile's processing origin.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: None for margin_pct -- pedagogical device for Challenge D2's dilation/scale-factor computation only.

sensitivity_note: margin_pct (15.0%) is directly and materially sensitive to MA4/MA5/MA6/MA7 taken together (Priya's shared monthly registration budget and how many concessions draw on it) and to MA3 (True Lock's achieved RMSE). It is comparatively insensitive to MA1, MA2, MA8, and MA9, which affect narrative color, D2/D4's geometry pedagogy, or Appendix D context without changing the D5 ratio's real inputs.

derived._note: Computed during this readiness pass from Appendix B/C/D/E's real+disclosed figures (FACILITATOR.md 'Data Deep Dive'); case-readiness/sensitivity_model.py should re-derive independently, not just trust this block.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA7 (5 concessions sharing Priya's fixed monthly registration budget) is a stated scenario count chosen to match Background's 'Kutai concession and several neighboring blocks' -- there is no public, fetchable record of how many concessions any specific fictional NGO analyst monitors, so this is an irreducible authorial choice, not a figure more research could pin down. Tier 2 probe 5's +/-50% sweep found this dial genuinely flips the resolved winner: at n_concessions=7.5 (+50%), the whole-month ratio favors Fast Lock (A) instead of True Lock (B), because a larger shared portfolio dilutes True Lock's Kutai-only benefit against a proportionally larger opportunity cost. At n_concessions=2.5 (-50%), True Lock's margin widens sharply (75%) toward the naive per-scene figure, because there are too few other concessions to absorb the opportunity cost. A facilitator running this case should treat the concession count as the single most load-bearing assumption in the whole-month resolution, exactly as case.json's own sensitivity_note and FACILITATOR.md's Anchor 4 / Thread 2 already flag it.
